strategy_rationale: Train and prediction periods are disjoint and chronological (train period_id range 2019-01..2025-05, prediction 2025-06..2025-12, 6 held-out monthly periods). The panel is structured as (period_id x jurisdiction x overdose_category). Holding out whole period_id blocks via GroupKFold on the time-block column mirrors the hidden evaluation: the hidden set never shares a period_id with training, and the evaluation metric (block_mae) is itself blocked on period_id. This dominates a plain time_based_holdout because GroupKFold over period_id guarantees every fold's validation rows come from periods entirely absent from that fold's training rows -- directly reproducing the train/val period disjointness -- while also yielding multiple folds (more stable OOF) instead of a single last-slice holdout.
simulates_hidden_evaluation: Each fold's validation rows are drawn from period_id values entirely excluded from that fold's training rows, reproducing the disjoint-period structure of train (2019-01..2025-05) vs hidden (2025-06..2025-12). block_mae is computed per period_id block in both OOF scoring and the hidden leaderboard.

leakage_risks.action: sample_submission.csv carries a placeholder target column for format only; prediction_file (val/covariates.csv) has no target -- not a leakage path, but feature code must never read the placeholder column from sample_submission.

leakage_risks.risk_type: high-cardinality non-datetime ID in feature set
leakage_risks.action: jurisdiction (51 levels) and overdose_category (8 levels) are valid grouping/feature keys for per-fold target aggregates, but any target-derived aggregate keyed on (jurisdiction, overdose_category) must be fit per training fold only, never on rows whose period_id falls in that fold's validation block.

leakage_risks.risk_type: train-only numeric columns strongly correlated with target (auxiliary categories)
leakage_risks.column: overdose_category (non-scored categories: heroin, fentanyl, cocaine, methamphetamine, benzodiazepine)
leakage_risks.action: These 5 unscored categories (corr 0.70-0.88 with scored categories, except heroin) exist in train for all period_id x jurisdiction combos but the prediction set only requires all_drugs/all_opioids/all_stimulants rows; using them as auxiliary signal (e.g. cross-category aggregates) is fine as long as aggregates are computed per fold on training-period data only and never leak validation-period target values.

Hidden prediction periods (2025-06..2025-12) are entirely beyond the max training period_id (2025-05); GroupKFold on period_id cannot fully replicate true future extrapolation -- monitor for drift in covariates (unemployment_rate, gtrends_*) across the 2025 horizon.

validation_limitations: GroupKFold over period_id holds out whole training periods but folds are drawn from within the 2019-01..2025-05 training span, not strictly the final periods -- it does not fully capture pure forward extrapolation to 2025-06..2025-12 (no training period exists beyond 2025-05, whereas validation folds here can include early/mid-range periods). Trend/seasonality extrapolation risk for the final 6-month horizon is therefore only partially represented by OOF error on these folds.
